title: Overview
text:
Cue My Music: Downloads 
 Find songs by name or link and save them into a resource pack for Cue My Music. 
 Search for a song by name on the  Downloads  page of the player, or paste a link there or into  /cmm download <link> , and the song is downloaded with  yt-dlp , converted to Ogg with  ffmpeg , and added to a resource pack called  Cue My Music Downloads . The pack is turned on for you, and the song shows up on the add-on's  Downloads  page in the player. 
 A playlist link downloads the whole playlist (up to 200 songs) and makes a Cue My Music playlist with the same name. An artist link downloads the artist's channel (up to 1000 songs) and adds them under the artist that Cue My Music already groups them by; downloading the artist again adds only the new songs. Spotify songs, albums, playlists and artists work too, through  spotdl , which reads the Spotify metadata while the audio still comes from YouTube. 
 Downloaded songs are add-on songs: they play in Cue My Music's  Add-ons  mode, which picks them in place of the game's music.  Vanilla + FX  leaves them out. 
 Only download what you have the right to. Many sites don't allow it in their terms. 
  Install ↗  GitHub Releases ↗

title: Install
text:
Install 
 Recommended: Prism Launcher   Create or select an instance with the Minecraft version and loader listed below.  Open  Edit → Mods → Download Mods . Find the mod on Modrinth or CurseForge where it is listed, and install its required dependencies.  If the mod is not listed there, download its JAR from the project’s release page and add it to the instance’s mods folder.  Complete the project-specific setup below, then launch the instance.    Get Prism Launcher ↗   Downloads    GitHub Releases     Client-side only. 
 
 Install  Cue My Music  1.3.0 or newer, with its requirements. 
 Install yt-dlp and ffmpeg. The add-on doesn't download them. 
 
  
 
 
 System 
 Command 
 
 
 
 
 macOS 
  brew install yt-dlp ffmpeg vorbis-tools  
 
 
 Windows 
  winget install yt-dlp.yt-dlp Gyan.FFmpeg  
 
 
 Linux 
 Your package manager, such as  sudo apt install yt-dlp ffmpeg . Distro yt-dlp packages are often too old for YouTube;  pipx install yt-dlp  gets the latest. 
 
 
  
 
 Put the jar from  Releases  in  mods . For Spotify links, also install spotdl:  pipx install spotdl  (or  pip install spotdl ). 
 
 The add-on looks for all three tools on your  PATH , and in  /opt/homebrew/bin ,  /usr/local/bin ,  /usr/bin ,  /snap/bin , and  ~/.local/bin  (on Windows, WinGet's  Links  folder), since launchers often don't pass on the shell's  PATH . A tool installed while the game is running is found on the next download. spotdl is optional; only Spotify links need it.

title: Use
text:
Use 
  Open the player and click  Downloads  in the library. The page has two tabs:  Download  for finding songs, and  Downloads  for the songs already saved. 
 On  Download , type a song or artist and press Enter or  Search . Songs come from YouTube Music's song search, official releases first: the top result as a card with its cover, then the rest with title, artist, album and length. Slowed, sped-up, lyric, cover and similar uploads go to the bottom unless you search for them. Click  Download  on the top result, or the arrow on a row; songs you already have show a tick, and a song being downloaded shows its progress.  Sort  reorders the results by relevance, plays, length or title, and  Show more  asks for up to 30 results. Past searches stay as buttons for the session. When the search is about an artist, an  Artist  card comes first, with  Download all  for their whole channel.  Clear  hides the results. If YouTube Music can't be reached, yt-dlp searches YouTube instead. To download from a link instead, paste it and press Enter or  Download . The tab shows the download's progress and has  Cancel  while it runs. If yt-dlp or ffmpeg is missing, it says which and shows the command to install it. 
 On  Downloads , your songs are listed below a filter box: type to narrow them by title or artist. Right-click a song and pick  Delete download  to remove it, or select several (shift-click) and press Delete.  Open folder  opens the pack's folder. A running download's progress shows on this tab too. 
 Spotify links are read with spotdl, then each song is matched to a YouTube Music result. A match that isn't clear (a remix, a live version, a different length) is shown with both titles, artists and lengths, and asks  Keep ,  Skip , or  Skip all ; the download waits until you answer.  Skip all  skips the rest of the uncertain matches in that link. Everything else downloads without asking. A Spotify playlist or album makes a Cue My Music playlist named after it; a Spotify artist adds the songs to that artist, like a YouTube artist link. 
 The same things work from chat: 
  
 
 
 Command 
 Does 
 
 
 
 
  /cmm download <link>  
 Downloads the song, or every song in a playlist, artist channel or Spotify link. Progress shows above the hotbar. When a Spotify match needs checking, the Downloads page asks Keep or Skip. 
 
 
  /cmm download cancel  
 Stops the download, and answers the match question with Skip. 
 
 
  /cmm downloads  
 Lists downloaded songs. Click the pack name to open its folder. 
 
 
  /cmm downloads remove <song>  
 Deletes a downloaded song. 
 
 
  
 
 One download runs at a time. 
 A video link that also names a playlist ( watch?v=…&list=… ) downloads just the video. Use the playlist's own link ( playlist?list=… ) for all of it. 
 Videos in a playlist that can't be downloaded (private, removed, region-locked) are skipped, and chat says how many. 
 Cancelling keeps the songs that had finished. 
 Spotify links need spotdl. Without it, the page and chat say how to install it. 
 Spotify matching searches YouTube Music, so a song that isn't on YouTube (or is there under a very different title) is reported as not found. 
 Live streams and anything over an hour are skipped. 
 The title is the track name if the site has one, else the video title. The artist is the site's artist, else the uploader (YouTube's "Artist - Topic" channels become "Artist"). Spotify downloads keep Spotify's title, artist and album. 
 Downloading the same song again replaces the old copy. Artist and Spotify links skip songs already in the pack. 
 
 Downloaded songs play in Add-ons mode only. With Cue My Music's defaults they also: 
 
  Automix:  play at matched loudness and blend into the next downloaded song over up to 8 seconds. 
  Stay out of recordings:  play from a separate process, so a recorder of the game's own audio (rec-util, or OBS's application audio capture) leaves them out, while game music and discs are still recorded. Recorders of all system audio still pick them up. 
 
 Both are in Cue My Music's  Settings  ( Automix add-on songs ,  Keep add-on songs out of recordings ). 
 After each download or removal, resources reload so the player sees the change.  That stops whatever is playing , as any resource reload does.

title: Configure
text:
Configure 
  The pack is a normal folder in  resourcepacks , so you can copy it to another game or share it: 
  resourcepacks/Cue My Music Downloads/
  pack.mcmeta
  pack.png
  assets/cuemymusic_dl/
    sounds.json        one sound event, cuemymusic_dl:music.downloads
    cuemymusic.json    each song's title, artist, album, and link
    sounds/music/*.ogg
  
 Files are named after the site's video id. 
 Sound quality 
 Minecraft only plays Ogg Vorbis, so every song is converted to it: stereo, at libvorbis's highest quality (10, about 400 kbps; a 5-minute song is about 15 MB). The source is already compressed (YouTube's audio is Opus at about 130 kbps), so converting again at anything less blurs drums and other sharp sounds you can hear. 
 That needs libvorbis. The Windows and Linux ffmpeg builds have it.  Homebrew's ffmpeg doesn't , so on a Mac install  vorbis-tools  as well ( brew install vorbis-tools ), which adds  oggenc , and the add-on uses that. Without either, ffmpeg's own Vorbis encoder is used, which sounds clearly worse; the Downloads page warns when that's the case. Songs already downloaded that way get the better encoding if you download them again. 
 To remove everything, delete the folder, or turn the pack off under  Options → Resource Packs .

title: Troubleshooting
text:
Troubleshooting 
   
 
 
 Problem 
 Fix 
 
 
 
 
  Couldn't find yt-dlp  or  ffmpeg  
 Install it with the command shown. If it's somewhere unusual, link it into  /usr/local/bin  or  ~/.local/bin . 
 
 
  Couldn't find spotdl , or a Spotify link says it needs it 
 Install it with  pipx install spotdl . The add-on looks in  ~/.local/bin  too. 
 
 
 A Spotify song matched the wrong video 
 Press  Skip  at the question. To skip every uncertain match in the link, press  Skip all . 
 
 
  Download failed  from YouTube 
 Update yt-dlp ( brew upgrade yt-dlp ,  winget upgrade yt-dlp.yt-dlp , or  yt-dlp -U ). Sites change often. 
 
 
 The song isn't in the player 
 Check that  Cue My Music Downloads  is on under Resource Packs. 
 
 
  
 yt-dlp's full output for a failed download is in  .minecraft/logs/latest.log .

title: Changelog
text:
Changelog  All notable changes to Cue My Music: Downloads are documented here. This project follows  Semantic Versioning . 
 [Unreleased] 
 Added 
 
  Tabs on the Downloads page , styled as the player's Mode switch:  Find songs  for search, links and progress, and  Downloaded  for the songs already saved, with a box to filter them by title or artist. 
 The Downloads pack has no picture any more: it looked like a player and stood in as every song's cover. 
  Song covers : every song gets its own cover, shown in Cue My Music: its album's cover from iTunes where it has the song, otherwise its YouTube thumbnail cut square. Songs downloaded before get theirs in the background, a few a minute, and thumbnails are swapped for album covers where one is found. 
  More search tools : sort results by relevance, plays, length or title;  Show more  for up to 30 results; and recent searches as buttons. 
 
 Fixed 
 
 Downloading outside Add-ons mode says to switch to Add-ons to play the songs. 
 The README no longer says downloads play from the player only: Add-ons mode picks them. 
 Downloading or deleting songs no longer reloads every resource (with a Cue My Music that has  CueSounds ): only the song list is read again, so it's quick and the song that's on keeps playing instead of skipping. 
 Downloading an artist no longer saves the same song twice when it's on both a single and an album, or is already downloaded. 
 
 [1.1.0] - 2026-10-28 
 Requires Cue My Music 1.3.0 or newer. 
 Added 
 
  Artist downloads : a YouTube channel or artist link, or an  Artist → Download all  card in search results, downloads the whole channel (up to 1000 songs). Songs already in the pack are skipped, so running it again only adds what's new. Cue My Music already groups them by artist, so no playlist is made. 
  Spotify links , through spotdl: songs, albums, playlists and artists. spotdl only reads the Spotify metadata; the audio comes from a YouTube Music match. Spotify playlists and albums make a Cue My Music playlist named after them. Install spotdl with  pipx install spotdl ; it's optional, and only Spotify links need it. 
  Check uncertain matches : when a Spotify song's YouTube match isn't clear (a remix, a live version, a different length), the Downloads page shows both and asks  Keep ,  Skip , or  Skip all  before continuing. 
 
 Changed 
 
 Shorter, plainer text: the Downloads page help, chat messages while downloading, and the mod list description. 
 Songs are converted to Ogg as each one finishes, not after the whole link, so long artist and playlist downloads use less disk and cancelling keeps the finished songs. 
 Spotify songs already in the pack are skipped, like artist downloads. 
 
 [1.0.0] - 2026-10-27 
 First release. Requires Cue My Music 1.3.0 or newer. 
 Added 
 
  Search by name : type a song or artist on the Downloads page. Results come from YouTube Music's song search, official releases first, with covers, and fall back to YouTube if YouTube Music can't be reached. 
  Downloads page  in the player, with progress, Cancel, a tick on songs you already have, and the list of downloaded songs. 
  Downloads into a resource pack  with yt-dlp and ffmpeg, from the Downloads page or  /cmm download <link> . 
  Playlists : a playlist link downloads every song (up to 200) and makes a Cue My Music playlist with the same name. Downloading it again adds only the new songs. 
  Delete several downloads at once : shift-click to select, then press Delete. 
  Sound quality : songs are encoded at libvorbis quality 10, through  oggenc  when ffmpeg lacks libvorbis. 
  Vanilla music : with Cue My Music's Vanilla music switch on, the  /cmm download  commands are hidden.

title: Develop
text:
Develop 
  Requires JDK 25 and a built Cue My Music in  ../cue-my-music  ( ./gradlew buildAll  there), which the add-on compiles against for playlists; see  gradle.properties . Then  ./gradlew build  builds the jar into  build/libs/ .
